seeds.context: Swoveralls sells overalls-style loungewear (Swoveralls, Swovie Shorts, Comfyalls, Corduroy and Grid Fleece versions) at $89-$159, with 41 core products, 26 of them limited edition and 24 new. It also has a Kids Swoveralls line at $43.99-$49 and merch at $25-$36, including Sidekick Tees and beanies and hats with slogans such as 'Free Your Waistband' and 'Good At Naps'. Fabrics seen are cotton, spandex and polyester, and the catalogue references pockets (5, 6 and 7). The playful naming and frequent limited drops are distinctive.
questions: Which ad hooks, formats and angles are performing best right now on Meta, TikTok and Instagram across the best consumer brands in any industry (apparel, DTC, food and drink, lifestyle), and how could Swoveralls, a playful overalls-style loungewear brand with limited drops, a kids line and slogan merch, adapt them to its own product and voice?

How do comfort-focused and loungewear brands such as The Oodie and Madepants advertise on Meta (creative formats, hooks, offers, UGC versus produced video, seasonal and gifting angles, limited-edition drop mechanics), and what gaps could Swoveralls exploit at its $89-$159 price point and with its kids line?
